cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Costs & Sustainability
cards.back: Material cost is a major factor in selection: raw material price, processing cost and stock form availability all affect the total cost.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Costs & Sustainability
cards.back: Economies of scale reduce unit cost: mass-produced components are cheaper per unit than one-off or small-batch production.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Costs & Sustainability
cards.back: Stock forms (bar, sheet, tube, extrusion) affect cost: standard sizes are cheaper than custom dimensions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Costs & Sustainability
cards.back: Waste material adds cost: near-net-shape processes (casting, moulding) reduce waste compared to machining from solid.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Costs & Sustainability
cards.back: Recyclability reduces long-term cost and environmental impact: metals are widely recycled; thermoplastics can be recycled; thermosets and composites are difficult to recycle.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Costs & Sustainability
cards.back: Planned obsolescence is designing products with a limited useful life to encourage replacement; this increases waste and resource consumption.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Costs & Sustainability
cards.back: Engineered lifespan means designing for a specific service life; maintenance schedules and replaceable components extend product life.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Costs & Sustainability
cards.back: End-of-life disposal must be considered: hazardous materials, landfill costs and regulations all influence material choice.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Costs & Sustainability
cards.back: Energy sources for production include fossil fuels, nuclear, wind, solar, tidal and biomass; renewable sources reduce carbon footprint.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Costs & Sustainability
cards.back: Life cycle assessment (LCA) evaluates the total environmental impact from raw material extraction through manufacture, use and disposal.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Costs & Sustainability
cards.back: Sustainable design minimises resource consumption, waste and pollution throughout the product's entire life cycle.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Material Costs & Sustainability
cards.back: The 6 Rs (Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Repair) guide sustainable engineering practice.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — material costs & sustainability?
cards.back: 1. For Material Costs & Sustainability questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4.
